## The shared root checkout stays on `main`

Many agents run **in parallel from the same root checkout** and spawn worktrees off it, so that checkout is shared infrastructure, not a workspace. Two rules follow, and both are about what your local tree does to *other* agents:

- **Never `git checkout` / `git switch` the root checkout to a work branch.** Its branch is the base every other agent branches from; moving it silently puts all of them on the wrong base.
- **Never edit tracked files in it** — not even a throwaway experiment you mean to revert. `docker-test.sh` / `docker-eval.sh` build images **from the current tree**, so an uncommitted edit contaminates every other agent's run, and untangling it later needs a conflict-resolved transplant.

**Do branch work in a linked worktree** — [`.agents/skills/plan-build-isolated/SKILL.md`](../.agents/skills/plan-build-isolated/SKILL.md) Phase 0. The trigger is the **first edit of a tracked file**, for any reason, not the intent to ship.

**Recovery — root checkout found off `main`:** commit any uncommitted work **on the branch it is currently on** first (that work belongs to whoever left it there) — **under its real `type(scope): summary` subject, never `WIP` / `fixup!` / `squash!`**, because that commit is publishable the moment it is pushed and GitHub's squash merge takes its subject rather than the PR title, so anyone with merge rights can land a `WIP` subject on `main` permanently (#9556; canonical statement, with the two measured instances: [`git-commit-secure`](../.agents/skills/git-commit-secure/reference.md) § *Never `WIP` as a subject*) — a `PreToolUse` hook (`commit-subject-guard.sh`, same backstop-not-guarantee terms as the root-checkout hook below) now denies a `git commit -m` whose subject starts that way, in Claude Code sessions — then:

```bash
git checkout main && git pull
```

**The `root-checkout-guard.sh` hook is a backstop, not a guarantee.** [`.agents/settings.json`](../.agents/settings.json) wires a `PreToolUse` guard that denies a root-checkout `git checkout`/`switch` to anything but `main` (git-native root detection: `--git-dir` == `--git-common-dir`; `git checkout main` and pathspec restores stay allowed; `INC_ALLOW_ROOT_CHECKOUT=1` disables it). It **matches command text**, so an aliased `git`, a wrapper script, or an unusual quoting shape evades it — it raises the cost of the accidental case, which is the one that actually happens. **Cursor ignores Claude Code hooks entirely.** The prose invariant above is the source of truth; the hook is one tool's enforcement of it. Limits and the offline deny/allow matrix: [`scripts/automation/hooks/README.md`](../scripts/automation/hooks/README.md).

## The prod pin: `deploy/prod-release.json`

[`deploy/prod-release.json`](../deploy/README.md) on `main` records what production runs: `{schema, sha, api_digest, frontend_digest, promoted_at}` — the promoted commit plus the **exact dev-validated image digests** pinned at promotion time. Digests are pinned when the promotion PR opens, so a later dev deploy moving `:dev-green` never changes what an in-flight promotion ships.

**Rollback = a one-line revert PR** re-pinning the previous `sha`+digests. A rollback (non-descendant pin) always requires a security-reviewer approval (see gate below).

## Daily promotion (bump PR)

Once per day (04:40 UTC) [`promote-prod-release-daily.yml`](../.github/workflows/promote-prod-release-daily.yml) checks whether the last-green `dev-deployed` commit is ahead of the pin. If so it resolves the `:dev-green` digests, force-pushes a **one-commit `prod-release-bump` branch** updating only the release file, opens a **bot-authored bump PR** (the `iudexnc-prod-promotion` GitHub App; label `promotion`) whose body embeds a **reviewable batch listing** (every PR in `old-pin..new-pin`, 🛑 `security-high` / ⚠️ `security-medium` tiers surfaced first — see below), and enables **auto-merge (squash)**. Review is **mandatory on every promotion** (#2628) — there is no unattended auto-promote path; see the gate below. The PR's one-file diff still matches almost no path-triggered workflow, so promotion doesn't re-run the batch's checks (the #1475/#1477 storm class is gone by construction).

If the bump PR is still open the next night, the workflow **refreshes it in place** (new pin + regenerated batch listing) rather than closing and reopening — unless the pin and digests are unchanged, in which case it skips the force-push entirely so an in-force approval on the current head survives.

Merging the bump PR triggers [`deploy-prod-release.yml`](../.github/workflows/deploy-prod-release.yml): import the pinned digests cross-registry dev→prod ACR (no rebuild — byte-identical), repin the prod apps, smoke, and advance the **`prod-deployed`** tag to the pinned commit. Re-running after a transient failure is `workflow_dispatch` on that workflow (re-applies the current pin; it never chooses a different commit).

## Mandatory security review gate (#2628)

One gate, and it is GitHub's own. The bump PR **merges unreviewed by design** (the pin is a sha dev already proved green); the mandatory approval is the `production` GitHub Environment's required reviewers on the **deployment** that merge triggers, so [`deploy-prod-release.yml`](../.github/workflows/deploy-prod-release.yml)'s `deploy` job (and any break-glass production dispatch) stops at *Waiting for review* (#4906). The workflow-based predecessor — the `Require security review` required check posted by `promotion-security-gate.yml` — was archived in #4905.

**What that archived status check enforced, and where each part lives now.** None of it holds the *merge* any more — the environment gate above does — but the batch listing and one offline guard survived the archive:

- **Every promotion still needs an approval from [@iudexnc/security-reviewers](https://github.com/orgs/iudexnc/teams/security-reviewers)** — given on the *deployment*, as the `production` environment's required-reviewers rule (`can_admins_bypass: false`, #4906), never on the PR: the bump PR merges on its own and `deploy-prod-release.yml`'s `deploy` job waits. There is **no unattended auto-promote path** (#2628 supersedes the earlier rule that engaged the gate only when the batch carried `security-high`). The archived check resolved team membership at runtime through a short-lived `iudexnc-automation` app token minted with org members:read (#5117 rotation completed 2026-08-07, the legacy `SECURITY_REVIEWERS_TOKEN` PAT fallback removed); the environment rule needs no such plumbing — GitHub evaluates the team itself — and no workflow mints that token for membership any more. An approval is bound to one deployment attempt, so a refreshed pin (a new bump-PR merge, a new deploy run) needs a fresh approval.
- **The batch listing survived.** [`promote-prod-release-daily.yml`](../.github/workflows/promote-prod-release-daily.yml) still derives the batch from the **release-file diff** (`old-pin..new-pin`) and scans those commits' source-PR labels via [`collect-batch-pr-labels.sh`](../scripts/ci/collect-batch-pr-labels.sh) (fail-closed on an incomplete scan, #1439) to render the listing in the PR body — a `security-high` PR is surfaced at the top of it ("review with extra care") and gets `Potasya` requested as reviewer, but does not change *whether* review is required.
- **The release-file-shape invariants** the check enforced — a bump PR touching anything besides `deploy/prod-release.json` refused outright; a **digest-only** change (same commit, different image bytes) and a **non-descendant pin** (rollback / history rewrite) flagged in its verdict — went with it: nothing in `promote-prod-release-daily.yml`, `deploy-prod-release.yml` or `render-promotion-batch.sh` re-checks them. The reviewer of the deployment reads them off the one-file diff and the batch listing.
- The head-branch contract between the opener and `deploy-prod-release.yml` is still enforced offline by [`test-promotion-branch-consistency.sh`](../scripts/ci/test-promotion-branch-consistency.sh) (#1489: an incompletely-swept head rename once silently bypassed the gate; #4905 shrank its consumer list from five to one when the gate cluster was archived).

**A deployment waiting on the native gate is silent** — no red check, no PR signal, prod simply does not advance. Two mechanisms announce it, and both are guarded ([`validate-prod-approval-announce-wiring.sh`](../scripts/ci/validate-prod-approval-announce-wiring.sh), the `prod_approval` suite in [`selftests.yml`](../.github/workflows/selftests.yml)): [`notify-prod-approval.sh`](../scripts/ci/notify-prod-approval.sh) posts a pointer comment + Google Chat ping from a gate-free job on **both** prod entry paths — and on a **drift / break-glass entry, where there is no promotion PR and the ping is the only channel, a failed send reddens that job** rather than concluding `success` over an announcement nobody received (#7815); the job is gate-free and un-`needs:`-ed, so that red never blocks the deploy it announces — and [`prod-approval-nudge.yml`](../.github/workflows/prod-approval-nudge.yml) polls `waiting` runs as the state-based fail-safe — 15 min for an attempt nothing announced, then hourly escalation. The poll is repo-wide on purpose (#7319), but `waiting` is the state of a hold on **any** gated environment, so what gets announced is scoped per run to `production` ([`should-announce-prod-approval-run.sh`](../scripts/ci/should-announce-prod-approval-run.sh), #7433).

- **Two mechanisms announcing is not two mechanisms *notifying*** (#7797). Both POST to the same Google Chat webhook, and both did so with a `curl` that lacked `--fail` — which exits 0 on any response it receives, 404 included. A revoked or rotated `GCHAT_DEPLOY_WEBHOOK` therefore reported a delivered ping on both paths at once, and the nudge's bucket dedup then recorded the run as *already pinged* and stopped retrying. Observed on run `32695943118` (2026-08-24), which waited 2 h with both channels green and no message sent. Both calls now pass `--fail-with-body`, so a non-2xx is a loud `WARN` naming the webhook — still advisory, because this must never fail a deploy, but no longer silent. **A shared channel makes the redundancy correlated: the fail-safe and the thing it backs up fail together.**

- **Operator rule: re-run a waiting prod deploy with a FULL `gh run rerun <id>`, never `--failed`** (#5624). A partial re-run re-enters the approval gate but does **not** re-run the pointer job (`--failed` re-runs only failed jobs and their dependents), so the deployment waits unannounced until the nudge fires. A full re-run re-announces, because the pointer's dedup marker is per run **attempt**.

# worktree goes, so the `.claude` symlink is never consulted. Measured on 2.1.220: with

#           hook_event_name, name (+ prompt_id for a subagent worktree). The public docs
#           also advertise `path` and `worktree_path`; this build sends NEITHER, so
#           nothing here may depend on them.
#   stdout: the worktree directory and nothing else — Claude Code cd's the session into
#           whatever this prints.

#           failure path therefore prints a diagnostic on stderr and exits non-zero:
#           a quiet success would drop the session into a directory that does not exist.

#   /Users/…/Projects/inc-b2c-mvp  ->  /Users/…/Projects/inc-b2c-mvp-wt/<name>
#   INC_WORKTREE_BASE_DIR=<dir> relocates the base wholesale (the shared VM exports
#   /mnt/worktrees, its data disk); export it in the shell that launches Claude Code.

# ~/.claude/hooks by install-guard.sh and fire in every repository, while this one is only
# ever wired from this repo's project-scoped `.agents/settings.json`.

# Offline matrix: test-worktree-create.sh (run by queue-selftest.yml).
set -euo pipefail

fail() {
  printf 'worktree-create: %s\n' "$1" >&2

# "invalid JSON" failure site that no control could ever reach, because the first parse
# has already proved the payload parses — a check whose pass is indistinguishable from
# a check that cannot run.
#
# A failed `jq` must be LOUD. Under `set -e` a BARE `parsed="$(… | jq …)"` aborts on its own
# (scoped-scripts.md) — silently, with no message naming the payload — and a DECLARED one would
# not abort at all, leaving $name empty and the worktree created at the base directory itself.
if ! parsed="$(printf '%s' "$input" | jq -r '[.name // "", .cwd // ""] | @tsv')"; then
  fail "payload is not valid JSON (fail-closed)"
fi

cwd="${parsed#*$'\t'}"
[ -n "$name" ] || fail "payload carries no .name (fail-closed)"

# The name lands in a path. Claude Code generates safe ones, but this hook is the thing
# standing between a payload and `git worktree add`, so it checks rather than trusts.
case "$name" in
  /*) fail "refusing worktree name '$name': absolute path" ;;
  *..*) fail "refusing worktree name '$name': parent-relative segment" ;;
esac
# `.` is a legal segment in Claude Code's own name schema, and it resolves to the
# BASE directory — which on the very first worktree is empty, so `git worktree add`
# would happily turn the shared `../inc-b2c-mvp-wt` root itself into a worktree.
# Slash-wrapping makes one pattern match every '.' segment position; a pattern led by
# a bare `.` reads as a `source` call to the transitive-source guard.
case "/$name/" in
  */./*) fail "refusing worktree name '$name': a '.' segment targets the worktree base directory itself" ;;
esac

[ -n "$cwd" ] && [ -d "$cwd" ] || cwd="$PWD"

# The MAIN checkout, asked of git rather than derived from a path comparison — and never
# taken from `cwd`: `cwd` is already a linked worktree whenever the session is isolated
# (measured — a subagent's payload carried the parent's worktree), and hanging the next
# worktree off THAT nests them one level deeper on every hop.
if ! common_dir="$(git -C "$cwd" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir 2>&1)"; then
  fail "not a git repository at $cwd: $common_dir"
fi
main_root="$(dirname "$common_dir")"

# INC_WORKTREE_BASE_DIR relocates the base: the offline matrix drives this against a fixture
# tree, and a host whose home disk is small points it at a data disk (the shared VM exports
# /mnt/worktrees). Unset, the behaviour is the sibling directory above.
base_dir="${INC_WORKTREE_BASE_DIR:-$(dirname "$main_root")/$(basename "$main_root")-wt}"
flat="$(printf '%s' "$name" | tr '/' '-')"
dir="$base_dir/$flat"

# A worktree whose branch is named `worktree-<something>` has to be renamed before it can
# become a PR (AGENTS.md § Branching wants feat/fix/chore/refactor), and renaming a branch
# is exactly the `git checkout`-shaped move that root-checkout-guard.sh denies. So a name
# that ALREADY carries a conventional prefix is taken as the branch name verbatim — ask for
# `fix/7373-thing` and that is the branch you get, ready to push.
case "$name" in
  feat/* | fix/* | chore/* | refactor/*) branch="$name" ;;
  *) branch="worktree-$flat" ;;
esac

# Reuse, not an error: Claude Code's own semantics for a name whose worktree already
# exists is "open that one", and a subagent re-entering its worktree must land back in it.
#
# Captured, not piped into `grep -q`: an external writer feeding a reader that stops early
# takes SIGPIPE, and under `pipefail` that 141 becomes the pipeline's status — a correct
# run reading as a failure (validate-pipefail-sigpipe.mjs).
worktree_list="$(git -C "$main_root" worktree list --porcelain)"
if grep -qx "worktree $dir" <<<"$worktree_list"; then
  printf '%s\n' "$dir"
  exit 0
fi

# Base ref mirrors Claude Code's `worktree.baseRef: "fresh"` default — branch from the
# remote's main so a new worktree starts clean. INC_WORKTREE_BASE_REF overrides it for the
# "carry my current work" case, the equivalent of baseRef: "head".
base_ref="${INC_WORKTREE_BASE_REF:-}"
if [ -z "$base_ref" ]; then
  if git -C "$main_root" rev-parse --verify --quiet origin/main >/dev/null; then
    base_ref="origin/main"
  else
    base_ref="HEAD"
  fi
fi

mkdir -p "$base_dir" || fail "could not create the worktree base directory '$base_dir'"

if git -C "$main_root" show-ref --verify --quiet "refs/heads/$branch"; then
  # Branch survives its worktree (a removed worktree leaves the ref): attach, don't -b.
  if ! add_out="$(git -C "$main_root" worktree add "$dir" "$branch" 2>&1)"; then
    fail "git worktree add '$dir' '$branch' failed: $add_out"
  fi
elif ! add_out="$(git -C "$main_root" worktree add -b "$branch" "$dir" "$base_ref" 2>&1)"; then
  fail "git worktree add -b '$branch' '$dir' '$base_ref' failed: $add_out"
fi

# `.worktreeinclude` is Claude Code's own mechanism for carrying gitignored files (.env.local
# and friends) into a new worktree — and it is documented as NOT processed once a
# WorktreeCreate hook takes over, so it is processed HERE instead. Without it every agent
# worktree starts with no dev credentials, the state in which deploy-dev.sh once stripped
# every dev secret because it read an .env.local that was not there.
include="$main_root/.worktreeinclude"
if [ -f "$include" ]; then
  while IFS= read -r pattern || [ -n "$pattern" ]; do
    case "$pattern" in '' | '#'*) continue ;; esac
    src="$main_root/$pattern"
    [ -f "$src" ] || continue
    # Gitignored files only — a tracked file is already in the fresh checkout.
    git -C "$main_root" check-ignore -q "$src" || continue
    # One failure site for the carry, not two: a separate `mkdir` diagnostic would be a
    # branch no control can reach (the destination's parent is a directory this hook
    # created moments ago), and a check whose red is unreachable is not a check.
    if ! mkdir -p "$dir/$(dirname "$pattern")" || ! cp "$src" "$dir/$pattern"; then
      fail "could not carry '$pattern' into the worktree"
    fi
  done <"$include"
fi

# stderr is free-form; stdout is the contract.
#
# The install command named here is `worktree-install-deps.sh`, never `npm ci` (#8200):
# a worktree's node_modules can be a directory of symlinks into the main checkout, and
# `npm ci` follows them and destroys MAIN's install. This is one of three places that
# printed the wrong remedy — the others are scripts/lib/deps-preflight.sh's diagnostic
# and plan-build-isolated/SKILL.md's step 5. Keep all three saying the same thing.
printf 'worktree-create: %s on branch %s (from %s). Run `./scripts/local/worktree-install-deps.sh` there before tests.\n' \

printf '%s\n' "$dir"

# Git push (`/gp`)

## Pre-flight

1. `gh auth status` (fails: `gh auth login`, GitHub.com, HTTPS, browser).
2. `git status --porcelain`. Anything uncommitted: run [commit-secure](../commit-secure/SKILL.md) first.
3. `bash scripts/check.sh` must be green. It is the gate: CI is on request and `main` has no branch

## Which mode

- **Push to main:** a small change inside your own module (see the module table in
  [docs/AGENT_DEVELOPMENT.md](../../../docs/AGENT_DEVELOPMENT.md)), or the user says "push directly".
- **PR:** you touch shared integration files (`pawse/app.py`, request/response models,
  `docs/openapi.json`, `schemas/pawse.ts`, requirements, README), or the user asks for a PR.

## Push to main

1. `git fetch origin && git pull --rebase origin main`. Conflicts: resolve, re-run the check,
   `git rebase --continue`. Unsure whose change wins: ask, do not guess.
2. `git push origin HEAD:main`.
3. Report the commit URL: `gh browse -n "$(git rev-parse HEAD)"` prints it.

## PR + squash-merge

1. **Existing PR?** `gh pr view --json number,url,state 2>/dev/null`. One open for this branch: push to it.
2. **On main?** Branch first: `git checkout -b <feat|fix|chore|docs>/<short-name>`.
3. **Sync:** `git fetch origin && git rebase origin/main`, then `bash scripts/check.sh`.
4. **Push + open:** `git push -u origin HEAD`, then `gh pr create --base main --title "<type: what>" --body-file <tmpfile>`
   using `.github/pull_request_template.md` (what changed, how verified, known gaps).
5. **CI only on request:** if the user asks for CI, `gh workflow run check --ref <branch>`, then `gh run watch`.
   Red: `gh run view <id> --log-failed`; fix, push, re-run.
6. **Merge:** after a green local check (and green CI, if it was requested), `gh pr merge <n> --squash --delete-branch`, then confirm
   `gh pr view <n> --json state` says `MERGED`.
7. Report the full PR URL (`https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/pull/<n>`), not just `#<n>`.

## Safety

- Never `git push --force` to `main`; on your own branch only `--force-with-lease`.
- Never merge with a red local check or a red requested CI run.

## Keep this skill current

Update when branch rules, CI checks or the merge method change. Run `python scripts/validate_skills.py` after editing.

# Secure commit

Small, frequent commits on a working state are the hackathon safety net: any broken build should be
one `git revert` away.

1. **Look:** `git status`, `git diff`, `git diff --staged`. Summarise the change in one line. If the diff

   stop: move the value to `.env` (git-ignored), re-run. Never weaken the scanner to pass.
4. **Check:** `bash scripts/check.sh`. Short on time: at least `python -m pytest -q tests`.
5. **Stage by name:** `git add <file> <file>`. No `git add -A` / `git add .` unless you read every file in
   `git status`.
6. **Commit:** `type: plain-English what` (feat/fix/chore/docs/test/research), e.g.
   `fix: clinic ranking keeps unknown opening hours unknown`. When an agent wrote most of it, end with a
   blank line and a `Co-Authored-By:` trailer naming the agent.
7. `git log -1 --stat` to confirm only the intended files went in.

## Safety

- A key that was ever pushed is leaked, even if a later commit deletes it: **rotate it** (event Gemini
  keys: one leaked key revokes every key in the project, see [gemini](../gemini/SKILL.md)).
- Never `--no-verify`, never `git commit --amend` on a commit that is already pushed.
- Never paste keys into commit messages, issues, or public pastebins/gists.

# Agent development

Development follows the product modules: frontend experience, orchestration, voice communication and evidence retrieval. Each module has a feature branch, an API boundary and a validation target. The current runtime is described in [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md). The next [multimodal design](MULTIMODAL_ARCHITECTURE.md#module-handoffs-and-build-order) assigns Voice, Vision, Document and evidence handoffs to these same modules.

Start integration work with [Controller–Frontend](controller-frontend-contract.md) and [Controller–Service](controller-service-contract.md). Detailed contracts are grouped by [Care](controller-care-contract.md), [Agents](controller-agent-contract.md), [Voice](controller-voice-contract.md) and [Knowledge/Data](controller-knowledge-contract.md). The [docs index](README.md) links the supporting provider and data references.

## Modules and branches

| Module | Branch | Source files | Deliverable | Validation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Frontend | `feat/frontend-experience` | `pawse/static/` | Mapify-inspired pink/gray UI; multilingual input, own-voice recording, agent progress, clinic cards and the Mimi rehearsal | Complete the story with keyboard or touch; show partial/error states; clearly distinguish simulated calls from live audio and API results. |
| LLM/orchestration backend | `feat/llm-orchestrator` | `pawse/orchestration.py`, `pawse/service.py`, `pawse/state.py`, assessment logic in `pawse/providers.py`, `pawse/demo.py`, orchestration tests | A bounded agent run, care guidance, explainable ranking, action gates and deterministic scenario costs | Independent providers start concurrently; urgent guidance survives provider failure; no invented booking, policy decision or deadline guarantee. |
